title: Drift Wood #11 · the Crab Derby
arc: French Cinema for the Indifferent / the Crab Derby
logline: Gully's uncle needs a flyer. Wood needs a subject. Everyone needs crab.

panels.composition: The boat launch. A shingle shack (Gully's UNCLE's — not Gully's yet). A hand-painted sign: 14TH ANNUAL CRAB DERBY. GULLY and WOOD in the rain with the uncle.

balloons.text: Gully says you draw. I need a flyer. Crab on it. Big.

image.prompt: a weathered shingle shack at a small-town boat launch in rain, a hand-painted crab derby sign, an older fisherman pointing at the wall, two teenage boys with a crab pot

panels.composition: Wood, considering the assignment with visible pain.

balloons.text: I was hoping to work in a more... Rohmer register. Quiet. Conversational. Crabless.

image.prompt: a teenage boy in an overcoat with his hand on his chin, pained, at a boat launch
close-up of a weathered fisherman's flat face in a rain hood

panels.composition: The flyer, taped to the shack. A crab so large and so carefully hatched it looks like an engraving. Below it, tiny: a Rohmer quote nobody will read.
props: the flyer on the shack wall with an enormous crab

image.prompt: a hand-drawn flyer taped to a wet shingle wall showing an enormous meticulously hatched crab, tiny text underneath, black and white
image.notes: The crab should be beautiful. That's the joke.

notes: The first commission. The first Crab Derby. Twenty bucks.
